name: Ronin Bridge (Ethereum side) 2024-08-06 - racer 3: 2.4173 ETH, a user's own withdrawal redirected
one_liner: Racer 3 copied a user's pending 2.4173 ETH Ronin bridge withdrawal, changing only the recipient, and landed first in the same block (user's own tx reverted at idx 258); no return of the take was found.
narrative: There is no hostile attacker. A governance upgrade of the bridge proxy (tx 0x855dd3b1..., 08:48:47) left withdrawals checked in a way that let a modified receipt pass; the first post-upgrade user withdrawals became bot bait. Three independent searchers each saw a legitimate user withdrawal (receipt ids 166631-166633) in the public mempool and sent a copy with the recipient (and for two of them the quantity) rewritten, ahead of it: ETH leg 0x26195700 (block 20468679 pos 0, 3,996.09375 ETH), a third racer 0x77bb83dd (block 20468790 pos 0, 2.4173 ETH, quantity unchanged) and Yoink 0xbce5b854 (block 20468848 pos 1, 1,998,046.875 USDC). Calldata diffs: ETH leg differs from the user's tx in 2 of 76 words, racer 3 in 1 of 67, Yoink in 3 of 61. All three were placed ahead of the user's tx, which stayed pending and later reverted.

fate.text: No return of the 2.4173 ETH was found in the saved Etherscan lists of the racer EOA and contract through 2024-08-06 22:00 (the take was forwarded to the EOA in the same tx; the EOA kept trading). Ronin sent this EOA the same on-chain text as the other two at 2024-08-06T11:02:59Z ('Hey, thanks a lot for white hat saving user funds today. Can we chat over Blockscan chat?'). Unknown != none: later activity was not traced.
